name: btc_regime_sizing_timeliness_riskchannel
status: Stage R COMPLETE — gate NOT passed (0/8 OOS cells). Lag-artifact hypothesis REFUTED. Overlay closes for a mechanism reason; bar-timeframe line closes with it. No PnL read spent.

stage_R_outcome.reconciliation_with_the_downgrade_audit: Recomputed czz4 is IDENTICAL to the stored states (counts 130776/97197/741 match exactly; the apparent mismatch was encoding, stored {0,1,2} vs causal_zigzag {-1,0,1}). Pooling VAL+OOS reproduces the audit's variance ratio to three decimals: 0.881, n=59, bear 34 / bull 25, mean bear +0.106% vs bull +1.143%.
stage_R_outcome.primary_finding: The audit's 0.881 is a POOLED number that averages two opposite behaviours. Split by window the variance ratio bear/bull is 0.097 on VAL (bear ~10x LESS volatile, Brown-Forsythe p=0.009 — SIGNIFICANT in the wrong direction) and 6.49 on OOS (bear ~6.5x MORE volatile, p=0.185 — not significant). A ~67x reversal. So the risk channel is not merely inverted, it is UNSTABLE: there is no stable risk relationship to size against in either direction.
stage_R_outcome.lag_hypothesis_refuted_twice: Earlier detection does not help and monotonically HURTS. single-slot OOS ratio 6.49 (5m) -> 6.10 (15m) -> 6.02 (30m) -> 3.89 (1h); n3 OOS 1.39 -> 1.30 -> 1.21 -> 1.06. Every coarse grid moves the ratio TOWARD 1, i.e. away from a usable risk signal. On VAL the 5m/15m/30m detectors produce identical trade labels (all 0.097), so at theta=4% detector speed barely differentiates where trades actually sit.
stage_R_outcome.consequence: The czz_trend sizing overlay has no risk mechanism at any detector speed. Combined with the effect-size downgrade (no significant mean effect, premise reverses VAL->OOS, permutation percentile backwards), the map's drawdown improvement is placement luck. The theta=3-4% learned-detector line also loses its only identified consumer.

status_note_original: PRE-REGISTERED — Stage R (risk channel), no learning, no PnL read
origin: User approved a timeliness contract to swap the czz_trend sizing overlay's input from 5m czz4 to 30m czz4, on the strength of Stage 0 finding that coarse grids detect theta=4% turns EARLIER (5m 985 min -> 30m 812.5 min, -17.5%).

why_the_scope_changed_before_the_first_r.new_information: The effect-size audit (project-btc-regime-sizing-effect-size-downgrade-20260808, scripts/audit_btc_regime_sizing_effect_size_20260808.py) DOWNGRADED the czz_trend overlay from ADOPTED to NOT-SUPPORTED: no mechanism is significant (mean p=0.33), the permutation percentile is 73.5% where the map was SELECTED vs 94.6% where it was not, the premise reverses sign VAL->OOS, and decisively the VOLATILITY CHANNEL POINTS THE WRONG WAY — variance ratio bear/bull = 0.881, i.e. bear-labelled trades are LESS volatile, so downsizing bear cannot cut drawdown through a risk channel.
why_the_scope_changed_before_the_first_r.consequence_for_the_approved_line: Swapping in a FASTER detector would make a rule whose premise is refuted fire SOONER. Measuring its PnL first would be optimising a component whose measured effect is placement luck.
why_the_scope_changed_before_the_first_r.the_hypothesis_that_survives: The 5m czz4 detection lag at theta=4% is 985 minutes (~16.4 h). A label that arrives 16 h late attaches 'bear' to the LATE, CALM tail of a down-wave while the volatile early part is still labelled 'bull'. So variance ratio 0.881 may itself be an ARTIFACT OF LAG rather than a fact about bear regimes. That is directly testable, and Stage 0 already measured that coarse grids cut the lag by 17.5%.
why_the_scope_changed_before_the_first_r.which_rule_this_follows: The downgrade's own reusable rule #2 — 'for a RISK claim, test the risk channel'. So the risk channel is tested FIRST, before any sizing or PnL measurement.

stage_R.question: Does a faster theta=4% detector flip the variance ratio bear/bull above 1?
stage_R.kind: no-learning labelling measurement on existing ledgers; no model trained, no sizing applied, no PnL read
detectors: czz4 on 5m (the incumbent the overlay reads)
stage_R.labelling: each trade is labelled by the detector state at its ENTRY-SIGNAL bar — identical to what the overlay does — so the only thing that varies across arms is detector timeliness

ledgers.single_slot_identity: continuity with the audit that produced the downgrade (n=59, 41 active OOS)
ledgers.n3_identity_m1.5: 3x the sample (124 gated OOS trades); small n is the downgrade's stated weakness, so the higher-power ledger is reported alongside

metrics_per_detector_per_ledger_per_spli: variance ratio bear/bull + Brown-Forsythe p (THE gate)
mean bear vs bull + Welch t + Cohen's d
bear share of negative return vs bear share of trades
bear occupancy (a detector that labels almost nothing bear can post any ratio)

gate.pass: at least one coarse detector reaches variance ratio bear/bull > 1.0 with Brown-Forsythe p < 0.10 on OOS, at bear occupancy >= 15% of trades
gate.occupancy_floor_reason: a detector that labels 3% of trades bear can post an arbitrary variance ratio; the floor is set at 15% because the overlay only does work when it actually downsizes a meaningful share
gate.on_pass: the lag-artifact hypothesis is supported and the overlay line reopens on a real mechanism — THEN, and only then, a second stage measures sizing and PnL with the faster input.
gate.on_fail: the premise is dead independently of detector speed. The czz_trend sizing overlay closes for a MECHANISM reason (not merely an effect-size one), and the bar-timeframe line closes with it. No PnL read is spent either way.

explicitly_not_in_this_stage: no PnL or MDD is computed
no live config is touched (the A/B shadow keeps running unchanged at 1.5x per the user's decision on the margin-multiplier provenance correction)
